answer: A haven that resists sybils charges every new agent a refundable stake held in escrow, like a pearl locked in a vault: one identity, one deposit. A zephyr of free accounts blows through unimpeded, but an attacker spawning ten thousand identities must lock ten thousand deposits, each slashed when the agent misbehaves. Honest agents earn the stake back with interest from fees, so the cost falls on the attacker, not the community. Sybil resistance becomes economics: faking identity is cheap only when it is free.
